key_catalyst: Rubio saying Iran is 'not serious about talks' as US strikes enter their 12th night, pushing Brent above $90-93 and the 10-year yield to 4.62%
reasoning: The dominant catalyst — US-Iran escalation driving Brent above $90 and the 10-year yield to ~4.62% — is a recurring theme rather than a novel shock: the identical setup appeared on 2026-07-20 (ninth day of strikes, Brent above $90, yields up) and QQQ still closed +0.10%, and the 4.60% yield print on 2026-07-16 was followed by a full recovery to record highs on 2026-07-21. The chip pullback is explicitly described by all three sources as profit-taking after Tuesday's 5-9.4% snapback rally, which is normal digestion rather than thesis damage, and the Alphabet/Tesla reports are a scheduled, known event that the market has been positioning into since 2026-07-20. Pre-market is down only 0.66% against impact-9 bearish framing, which reads as ordinary de-risking ahead of a binary event rather than the market failing to absorb something severe.
